document_title: ASAE Standards of Conduct / Code of Conduct
notes: Core Ethical Standards cover: basic conduct, confidentiality, competition, giving and receiving. ASAE is the meta-level governance body for association executives. Ethics Toolkit (2025): https://www.asaecenter.org/-/media/models-and-samples/6/6/1/5/ASAE-Ethics-Toolkit-March-2025.ashx. Standards PDF: https://www.asaecenter.org/-/media/ASAE/Files/AboutASAE/Standards-Of-Conduct-SEPT-23-2022.ashx

organization: American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations
notes: Applicable to all AFL-CIO workplaces, events, activities, meetings. Covers anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, professional conduct. PDF: https://aflcio.org/sites/default/files/2018-02/AFL-CIO%20Code%20of%20Conduct%20-%20Final.pdf. AFL-CIO Constitution (Article X) also requires affiliated unions to adopt own ethical practices codes. Represents 12.5 million members.

All CompTIA-certified persons must agree to this code. Covers: no dishonesty/fraud/deceit; no unauthorized IT system breach; no cheating. A+ and other CompTIA certs are common in Div. 95 repair roles. CROSS-LISTING: also appears in J62 (ICT) for cybersecurity context.

Membership prerequisite. Two tiers: Principles of Ethics (aspirational) and Rules of Ethics (mandatory). Covers client welfare, professional conduct, confidentiality, scope of practice. PDF: https://tn.wp.amtamassage.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/50/2011/03/code_of_ethics_AMTA.pdf

document_title: ABMP Code of Ethics for Massage Therapists
notes: Second major US massage therapy membership organization. Code covers client dignity, confidentiality, professional boundaries, scope of practice. Membership binding. Parallel to AMTA code.
Covers client confidentiality, scope of practice, professional conduct, honest representation of qualifications, legal compliance. NCEA Certified (NC) credential linked.

PBA absorbed the National Cosmetology Association (NCA). Separate codes for manufacturers, distributors, salon/spa owners, licensed professionals (pledge at probeauty.org/pledge). Covers health/safety standards, professionalism, ethical behavior. NCA heritage incorporated.

CROSS-LISTING: also classifiable under G47 (Retail, mortuary goods). Code covers obligations to: the family, care of decedent, public, government, NFDA members. PDF: https://nfda.org/Portals/0/NFDAORG/About/Professional_Conduct/Code-of-Professional-Conduct.pdf. Approved October 19, 2002.

Sets values, principles, and standards for Certified Matchmakers. Core values: customer service, dignity of person, importance of human relationships, integrity, competence. Covers responsibilities to clients, colleagues, practice settings, and the profession. Addresses client self-determination.
